issue.title: aws_eks_cluster reports recurring drift when AWS automatically updates platform_version
issue.body:
### Terraform and AWS Provider Version

```console
Terraform version: Any / Latest
AWS provider version: Any / Latest
```

### Affected Resource(s) or Data Source(s)

- `aws_eks_cluster`

### Expected Behavior

AWS-managed changes to platform_version should not be reported as actionable
configuration drift, because:
The attribute is read-only/computed.
Users cannot select or pin an EKS platform version.
AWS upgrades it automatically.
The Kubernetes minor version remains pinned and unchanged.
Terraform cannot revert the platform version.
Ideally, the provider should treat this attribute in a way that prevents
AWS-managed platform updates from producing recurring drift notifications,
while continuing to expose the current platform version as a readable
attribute.
If provider-level suppression is not technically possible, guidance on the
recommended approach for drift-detection platforms would be appreciated.

### Actual Behavior

The provider refresh reports the AWS-managed platform version update as
out-of-band resource drift:
platform_version = "eks.23" -> "eks.24"
The user cannot configure or pin platform_version through the EKS API.
When aws_eks_cluster is created by a child module, users also cannot attach a
resource-level lifecycle.ignore_changes rule from the parent module.
A refresh-only state synchronization temporarily clears the drift, but it
returns whenever AWS performs another automatic platform update.

### Relevant Error/Panic Output

```console

```


### Sample Terraform Configuration

terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "<insert version>"
    }
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region = "eu-central-1"
}

resource "aws_eks_cluster" "this" {
  name     = "example"
  version  = "1.34"
  role_arn = aws_iam_role.cluster.arn

  vpc_config {
    subnet_ids = var.subnet_ids
  }
}



### Steps to Reproduce

- Create an EKS cluster with a pinned Kubernetes minor version.
- Run terraform apply or tofu apply.
- Wait for AWS to automatically advance the EKS platform version.
- Run terraform plan, tofu plan, or a refresh-only drift check.
- Observe platform_version reported as a change made outside Terraform.
- The same behavior can be reproduced by importing or refreshing a cluster whose
- platform version has changed since the state was last written.

### Debug Logging

This is particularly problematic in compliance environments where any
out-of-band change reported by Terraform is treated as a failed drift
check.
Using -refresh=false is not an acceptable workaround because it would also
hide genuine infrastructure drift. Repeated refresh-only state updates reduce
the reporting window but do not resolve the recurring behavior.


### GenAI / LLM Assisted Development

n/a

### Important Facts and References

AWS EKS automatically upgrades the platform version of an existing cluster
without changing its Kubernetes minor version.
The AWS provider exposes platform_version as a computed attribute on
aws_eks_cluster. When AWS performs an automatic platform upgrade, every
subsequent refresh detects the remote value changing from the value stored in
state.
For example:
Note: Objects have changed outside of Terraform

# aws_eks_cluster.this has changed
~ resource "aws_eks_cluster" "this" {
    name             = "apps-dev-sandbox"
  ~ platform_version = "eks.23" -> "eks.24"
}
The configured Kubernetes version remains unchanged:
version = "1.34"
No user, Terraform run, or external infrastructure automation changed
the cluster. The change was performed automatically by the EKS service.
This causes recurring false-positive drift reports in automated drift-detection


### Would you like to implement a fix?

No
